title: Grace Bedell Tells Lincoln to Grow a Beard
text:
In October 1860, a few weeks before the presidential election, an eleven year old girl in Westfield, New York, named Grace Bedell wrote to the Republican candidate, Abraham Lincoln. She had seen his picture and thought his face was very thin. If he let his whiskers grow, she wrote, he would look a great deal better, and since all the ladies liked whiskers, they would tease their husbands to vote for him.

Lincoln answered her himself on October 19. He said he had no daughter, only three sons, and asked whether people would not think it a piece of silly affectation if he began wearing whiskers now, having never worn any. But soon afterward he stopped shaving.

In February 1861 the new President's train to Washington stopped at Westfield. Lincoln told the crowd that he had a correspondent there and asked for Grace Bedell. She was brought forward, and he stepped down from the platform, told her he had let his whiskers grow for her, and kissed her. He became the first American president to wear a beard.
lesson: Take seriously the advice of people who seem to have no standing to give it. Respect shown to a child, or to anyone small, is long remembered.
location: Westfield, New York, and Springfield, Illinois, USA
source: Grace Bedell, letter to Abraham Lincoln, October 15, 1860; Lincoln, letter to Grace Bedell, October 19, 1860, Collected Works of Abraham Lincoln, vol. 4
